title: Dice-Fairness Audit for the Table
dataSources: Campaign sessions (`campaign:session`), NPC ledger (`npc:ledger`), loot drops (`loot:drop`), XP awards (`xp:award`).
app: Tabletop RPG telemetry — virtual-tabletop session logs (Roll20, Foundry VTT), campaign trackers (World Anvil), and XP / loot / NPC ledgers — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=xp:award event=roll
| stats count as rolls, avg(d20) as avg_roll by player
| eval expected=10.5, deviation=round(avg_roll-expected,2)
| where rolls>=30
| sort - deviation
description: Audits each player's long-run d20 average to check whether a lucky-feeling set of dice is actually skewed.
value: Over enough rolls, a genuinely biased die shows up; this settles good-natured accusations at the table with data.
implementation: Ingest roll data into `index=personal`; compare each player's average to the expected value.
visualization: Bar chart of average roll deviation by player.
grandmaExplanation: It checks whether anyone's dice are genuinely lucky or unlucky over many rolls, settling table debates.
